status: BASE ONLY, built from vendored source. A7670E 4G, GNSS, camera and SD features NOT yet present.
summary: Flash the ESP32-S3 router firmware directly from the browser. No command line or Python installation required.
upstream_license: NOT DECLARED - upstream repo has no LICENSE file and GitHub reports license=null. Only the vendored WireGuard submodule carries an explicit BSD-style licence. Redistribution terms must be clarified with the author before any product release.
base_note: Built from the vendored esp32_nat_router 2.4.17 source in this repository, not upstream's prebuilt image. AP SSID broadcasts as NomadLink and the mDNS hostname is nomadlink.local. The A7670E 4G, GNSS, camera and SD features are not yet in this image.
prereq_note: Recommended: Chrome, Edge or Opera. Close all other serial monitors first. Browser flashing writes bootloader, partition table, otadata and app.

verification.web_installer_mount: PASS - esp-web-install-button custom element defined, manifest attribute set, button visible (Chrome)
verification.manifest_and_binaries_served: PASS - HTTP 200 for manifest and all four parts at the declared offsets; sizes 17664 / 3072 / 8192 / 1370000 bytes match the manifest
verification.actual_flash_to_device: PASS - flashed by the project owner from the published web installer on 2026-10-01; AP broadcast SSID 'NomadLink'. Recorded as TEST-810.
verification.on_device_runtime: PASS for the base path - boots, broadcasts 'NomadLink', and a client behind the AP reaches the internet (owner-confirmed, TEST-810), so SoftAP + DHCP + NAPT + forwarding + STA uplink all work. Not measured: throughput in Mbps, load behaviour. No 4G/GNSS/camera/SD in this image.
verification.vendored_source_compiles: PASS - make product: nat_router ok (ESP-IDF 5.5.4, app binary size 0x14f970 / 1374576 bytes)

verification.served_binary_is_local_build: PASS - payload staged by scripts/project-tracker/stage-firmware.sh from build_esp32s3, offsets asserted against flash_args (0x0/0x8000/0xf000/0x20000)
verification.branding_in_flashed_bytes: PASS - in nomadlink.bin: 'NomadLink' 4 occurrences; 'ESP32 NAT Router' 0; 'ESP32_NAT_Router' 0; 'esp32-nat-router' 0. Checked by scanning the staged payload, not the source.

toolchain: ESP-IDF 5.5.x (installed at ~/esp/esp-idf-5.5.4). The base does NOT build on IDF 6.x: main requires component 'json', which moved to the component manager.
stage_command: make stage-firmware  (rebuilds and re-stages the served payload; offsets verified against build_esp32s3/flash_args)

branding.firmware_artifact: nomadlink.bin (IDF project renamed from upstream's esp32_nat_router)
branding.note: The MQTT topic prefix stays esp32_nat_router: it is a functional broker identifier, not branding, and renaming it would break existing subscriptions.

reproducibility: NOT byte-reproducible, by upstream design: CMakeLists.txt force-rebuilds esp_app_desc.c so __DATE__/__TIME__ stay current. Two builds of identical source differ in ~67 bytes of the app descriptor only, same length. Do not treat a hash mismatch as a corrupt payload; the freshness guard is timestamp-based for this reason.
ui_present_in_base: /config (full config incl. uplink ssid/password, static IP, AP settings)
ui_still_to_build: A WiFi-vs-4G uplink selector - the base hard-assumes the STA is the only uplink, so this concept does not exist yet
rollback_note: Serves the TEST-810 verified base again (0.1.0-base.1, 1374544 B). A 4G-uplink build (0.2.0-4g.1, 1428944 B) was published on 2026-10-01 and then withdrawn: it did not bring up the SoftAP, so no NomadLink AP was visible and the device was unusable. Root cause localised to code running before the AP starts (esp32_nat_router.c:1633) but not yet isolated. The 4G work is retained in history at commit 8b09974.
